refnamediv.refpurpose: run a program under a pseudo-terminal

refsection.title: Description
refsection.para: pty-run is a utility that expects file descriptor 4 to be the back end (called master side in older documentation) of a pseudo-terminal and the TTY environment variable to be the full device filename of the front end. (pty-allocate1 can be used to set this process state up.)
It spawns next-prog, closing the back-end file descriptor in the child process, and then enters a loop where it simultaneously:

listitem.para: writes all data received from the back end to its own standard output, until the back end signals hangup (i.e. when the line discipline would set modem control lines, as it would on a real serial device, to signal hangup because the last front-end file descriptor is closed);
writes all data received from its standard input to the back end, until its standard input signals EOF with a 0 byte read; and
acts upon state changes in the spawned child process.
If the -t option was used, it behaves in pass-through TTY mode.

It copies the terminal mode settings from its standard input or output to the pseudo-terminal and sets both its standard input and output to raw mode. If the child process stops with a stop signal, it undoes this and stops itself. When it receives a SIGCONT, it re-does it and sends a SIGCONT to its child.
In the default if the -t option is not used, it behaves in pipe mode.
It makes no alteration to terminal mode settings. If the child process stops with a stop signal, it simply sends it a SIGCONT immediately.

refsection.para: next-prog may contain its own command‐line options, which pty-run will ignore.

refsection.title: Security
refsection.para: pty-run does not touch the front-end device at all. The front-end device race condition that must be avoided for open-controlling-terminal1 (q.v.) and similar front-end programs should have already been handled by whatever created the pseudo-terminal (e.g. pty-allocate1).

listitem.para: an I/O pump that pumps data in both directions between the back end of a pseudo-terminal and an abstraction of a virtual terminal's display and human input device hardwares
